quotes.text: Mr. Banks’ panama hat was in one hand, while the other drew a handkerchief across his perspiring brow.
quotes.reference: 1913, Robert Barr, chapter 5, in Lord Stranleigh Abroad:

quotes.text: Iron and coal were the magnets that drew railways to this land of lovely valleys and silent mountains—for such it was a century-and-a-half ago, before man blackened the valleys with the smoke of his forges, scarred the green hills with his shafts and waste-heaps, and drove the salmon from the quiet Rhondda and the murmuring Taff.
